11 passing. Now the refactoring analysis.

**Step 1 — Naming evaluation (first priority)**

| Name | Does it reveal intent? |
|---|---|
| `percentOf` | Yes — `percentOf(10, 100)` reads as "10 percent of 100". |
| `roundPremiumInMHPCOsFavour` | Yes — encodes the domain rule, not just `ceil`. |
| `basePremiumForItem`, `sumBasePremiums`, `blockBasePremium`, `policyBasePremiumFor` | Yes. |
| `quoteFor` | Yes. |
| `itemsFormASingleBlock` | **No.** This is the one weak name. It claims "the items form a single block", but the predicate also silently requires the components be *runes* — a hardcoded type from the Green phase. A caller reading the name would expect `[moonstone, moonstone, moonstone]` to be true; it returns false. The name over-promises relative to the behaviour, and the comment above it is doing the work the name should do. |

The hardcoded `"rune"` is scaffolding the next test will delete, so I should not generalize it (that would implement ahead). But I can make the name honest about the narrowness rather than leaving the discrepancy buried in a comment.

**Step 2 — Current APP mass** (`itemsFormASingleBlock`, the target):

| Component | Count | Mass |
|---|---|---|
| Constants (`BLOCK_SIZE` ref, `"rune"`) | 2 | 2 |
| Bindings (`items`, `item`) | 2 | 2 |
| Invocations (`every`, 2× `===`, `.length`, `.type`) | 5 | 10 |
| Conditionals / loops / assignments | 0 | 0 |
| **Total** | | **14** |

Let me make the rename, which is Rule 2 (reveals intent) and outranks any mass consideration.

content.text:
Refactoring complete. Lint clean, typecheck clean, 11/11 tests green.

## Refactoring applied

**1. Naming (Rule 2 — reveals intent), the primary change**

`itemsFormASingleBlock` → `itemsAreExactlyOneBlockOfRunes` in `/home/experimenter/experiments/runs/2026-08-17_07-18-23_claim-office-example-mapping_v6.2-with-why-cleaned_opus-5-no-thinking/src/claim-office.ts`

The old name over-promised. It read as a general block predicate, but the body also requires every component be a `"rune"` — so `[moonstone, moonstone, moonstone]` returns false, contradicting what a caller would infer from the name. The discrepancy was documented only in a comment; the name now carries it. I deliberately did **not** generalize to grouping by component type, per your instruction — the next test drives that, and the honest name makes the scaffolding visible so it's obvious what to delete.

Mass unchanged at 14 (pure rename). Rule 2 outranks APP, and this was a clarity-only win.

**2. Pre-existing typecheck failure — found via `tsc`, not visible from `pnpm test`**

This one is worth your attention. `npx tsc --noEmit` was failing with **11 errors**, all in the spec file, and had been before I touched anything:

```
src/claim-office.spec.ts(9,17): error TS2353: 'op' does not exist in type '{ items: Item[]; }'.
src/claim-office.spec.ts(20,36): error TS2353: 'material' does not exist in type 'Item'.
```

The `Scenario` and `Item` types omitted `customer`, `op`, `material`, `enchantment`, and `cursed` — fields every test already passes. Vitest transpiles without typechecking, so the suite ran green while `tsc` was red; the type safety the project rules call for was effectively off for this file. I widened both types (item attributes optional, `Step` extracted). No behaviour added and nothing new is priced — the fields remain unread, so this isn't implementing ahead. `customer.yearsWithMHPCO` and `op` are load-bearing for the loyalty-discount and second-quote tests coming up.

**3. Magic number (lint)**

`percentOf` tripped `no-magic-numbers` on its `100` divisor; extracted as `PERCENT_WHOLE`, which also names why the division exists.

One note for the next cycle: nothing currently reads `step.op`, so a `claim` step would be silently priced as a quote. The claim tests will force that distinction — flagging it rather than acting on it now.
